items.title: ASUU faults FG, states over unpaid salaries, 2025 agreement
items.description: By James Ogunnaike The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), has faulted the Federal and state governments over the continued non-payment of three-and-a-half months’ salaries withheld from university lecturers and the uneven implementation of the December 2025 agreement with the union. ASUU President, Prof. Christopher Piwuna, disclosed this while speaking on Frontline, a current affairs programme on Eagle 102.5 FM, Ilese-Ijebu. Pawn said the union had expected the agreement reached with the Federal Government in December 2025 to usher in greater stability in the university system, improve lecturers’ welfare and address longstanding challenges confronting public universities. He, however, expressed disappointment that several provisions of the agreement had either not been implemented or were being implemented inconsistently by the Federal and state governments. “It’s really painful to have a conversation on issues like this. Our expectation, when we signed an agreement in December 2025, was that we are going at this time to talk about the progress that we have made, the stability in the system and concern ourselves with issues that affect Nigerians,” he said. The ASUU president said the agreement covered improved salaries, funding for public universities and research support, among other provisions, but maintained that implementation had fallen short of the union’s expectations. Piwuna also raised concerns over the continued withholding of part of the salaries owed lecturers from the previous administration, saying three-and-a-half months out of the seven-and-a-half months withheld were still outstanding. According to him, the Federal Government had paid four months of the withheld salaries, leaving a balance of three-and-a-half months. He said the outstanding salaries remained a major source of concern for affected lecturers, adding that the union expected the government to resolve the matter. Beyond the withheld salaries, Piwuna said some universities were still facing difficulties implementing the new salary structure, while lecturers in some institutions remained uncertain about the payment of their full entitlements. “As we stand now, funding is not properly being done according to what was agreed to. Individual universities have to embark on strike before salaries are being paid. Some universities are cut off from the new salary structure,” he said. The ASUU president said the implementation challenge was not restricted to the Federal Government, noting that state governments also had obligations towards universities under their control. He said while some state governments had commenced implementation of the December agreement, others had yet to fully comply, resulting in disparities in the conditions of service across public universities. Piwuna cited Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, as one of the governors who had commenced implementation of the agreement. “Only Governor Alex Otti of the South-Eastern part has implemented it,” he said. He urged other governments to fulfil their commitments, stressing that ASUU had continued to engage relevant government officials through meetings and correspondence rather than immediately resorting to industrial action. “We have engaged them; the Minister of Education at federal level, we engaged Senator Larry Tejuosho, the chairman of the implementation committee monitoring the Federal Government agreement. We have reminded them to do the needful,” Piwuna said. On funding for education, the ASUU president said inadequate financing remained one of the major challenges confronting Nigeria’s public university system, particularly in the areas of research, infrastructure and human capital development. He called for sustained investment in education, arguing that adequate funding was essential if Nigerian universities were to produce research and innovation capable of competing in the global knowledge economy. Piwuna said governments should work towards dedicating up to 26 per cent of their annual budgets to education, describing such spending as an investment in national development rather than an expenditure that should continually be reduced because of competing demands. “Every government should at least aim to supply or to fund their budget or dedicate their budget up to 26 per cent to education, and Nigeria is not an exception,” he said. He, however, disclosed that ASUU had compromised during negotiations with the Federal Government by agreeing to a 15 per cent education budget benchmark, while recognising the financial difficulties involved in achieving the higher target immediately. “So while negotiating with the government, we told the government to reduce the budget to 15 per cent and they agreed. Although it may be difficult, it can be done incrementally,” he said. Piwuna said the agreement reached in December 2025 contained specific provisions for funding public universities, improving lecturers’ salaries and establishing mechanisms to strengthen research. “The agreement, when we signed it, had provision for funding for public universities. It had provisions for improved salary, and it had provision for research council, amongst others,” he said. He stressed that stronger investment in research was necessary for Nigerian universities to contribute meaningfully to national development and generate knowledge capable of competing beyond the country. According to him, underfunding the education sector has implications not only for universities but also for research, innovation, human-capital development and the wider economy. “We all know the value of education and we expect our leaders to carry out policies and actions that will promote education,” he said. Piwuna said ASUU remained committed to dialogue with the Federal and state governments but urged the authorities to address the outstanding issues surrounding lecturers’ salaries, the implementation of the December 2025 agreement and funding for public universities. items.title: Économie sociale et solidaire et Responsabilité sociétale des entreprises : Vers un cadre de concertation renforcé
items.description: Le ministre Alioune Dione a présidé, ce mardi 15 septembre, à Dakar, la première session 2026 du cadre de concertation de l'économie sociale et solidaire(Ccess). La rencontre va permettre d'aller vers une cadre de concertation renforcé. Le ministre de l'économie sociale et solidaire, Dr Alioune Dione, a présidé la première session 2026 du cadre de concertation de l'économie sociale et solidaire. La session a été consacrée notamment à la validation des versions finales de la Stratégie nationale d'encouragement à la Responsabilité sociétale des entreprises (Sn-Rse). De l'avis du ministre, cette session est d'autant plus plus importante qu'elle favorise la mise en œuvre de la loi d'orientation sociale numéro 2021-28 relative à l'Ess et pour la réalisation de la vision Senegal 2050. » Cette session intervient à un moment décisif de notre démarche visant à doter notre pays de cadres stratégiques solides, cohérents et opérationnels pour accélérer le développement de l'Ess et renforcer la Rse ». Selon Dr Alioune Dione, cette étape déterminante dans la mise en œuvre de ces deux stratégies nationales permet de consolider les acquis, de renforcer la cohérence des orientations et de permettre l'adoption et la mise en œuvre effective de ces instruments. Pour le ministre, cette session invite à penser l'Ess autrement, c'est à dire une économie qui crée des opportunités pour les jeunes et pour les femmes et qui valorise les initiatives locales et le savoir-faire de nos territoires. » Il urge de créer davantage de synergies entre performance économique, responsabilité sociale, impact territorial et développement durable », a dit le ministre de la Microfinance et de l'économie sociale et solidaire. Poursuivant il a souhaité que cette session soit celle de la maturité collective et de la décision, de la pertinence des orientations stratégiques proposées afin de répondre effectivement aux défis et opportunités de l'Ess et la Rse dans notre pays. Djibril NDIAYE

items.title: Diphtérie: un décès enregistré à Kaolack !
items.description: La diphtérie gagne du terrain dans la région de Kaolack. Selon la Direction régionale de la Santé, quatre cas ont été enregistrés à ce jour, dont un décès. La directrice régionale de la Santé, Dr Aïssatou Barry Diouf, a fait le point sur la situation de la diphtérie dans la région. « Nous avons enregistré quatre cas de diphtérie dans la région de Kaolack, dont malheureusement un décès », a-t-elle déclaré. Face à cette situation, la Direction régionale de la Santé appelle les populations à la vigilance et à consulter rapidement dès l’apparition de signes évocateurs. « Le mieux, c’est de recourir aux soins devant tout cas d’angine ou de mal de gorge, de difficultés à avaler ou à respirer. Il faudra également avoir la même attitude en cas de taches blanchâtres au fond de la gorge ou au niveau du nez », explique Dr Aïssatou Barry Diouf. Selon elle, en présence de ces symptômes, il est recommandé de se rendre dans la structure de santé la plus proche afin qu’un prélèvement puisse être effectué. « La diphtérie est une maladie à prévention vaccinale. J’exhorte les mamans et les gardiennes d’enfants à compléter la série vaccinale des enfants incomplètement vaccinés, mais également à démarrer la vaccination des enfants qui n’ont jamais été vaccinés », a-t-elle insisté. Dr Aïssatou Barry Diouf est également revenue sur le mode de transmission de la maladie, tout en invitant les populations à adopter les comportements appropriés. « C’est une maladie à transmission aérienne, à travers la parole, l’éternuement ou même les gouttelettes de salive qui sont projetées. Le port du masque peut aussi protéger la personne contre cette maladie », a-t-elle ajouté. Mamadou THIAM (Correspondant)

items.title: GSA delays laboratory equipment replacement despite available funds
items.description: The Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) says delays in government approval and authorisation processes are preventing it from replacing ageing laboratory equipment despite having funds available for the procurement. Director-General of the GSA, Prof. George Agyei, said the delays could affect the Authority’s ability to test and certify products for export markets if the situation persists. Speaking at the Authority’s 2025 Annual Stakeholder Meeting, Prof. Agyei appealed to the Ministry of Finance to expedite the necessary approvals to allow the GSA to retool its laboratories. “We have the money, but the process didn’t allow us to purchase the equipment on time.” He said the GSA’s laboratories operate according to international standards and are regularly subjected to inspections and audits, making reliable and modern equipment critical to maintaining their accreditation. Prof. Agyei warned that failure to meet the required standards could result in the loss of certification and accreditation, potentially affecting Ghanaian exporters. “If we don’t meet the required standards, our certification and accreditation will be taken away. And when these things are taken away, it means Ghana cannot export.” He explained that products such as fruits destined for international markets must undergo laboratory testing for contaminants, including pesticide residues and heavy metals. “If these things are not tested, it means those fruits cannot get access to our global market.” Most Ghanaian products meeting standards Despite the equipment challenges, Prof. Agyei said the GSA had recorded positive results in the quality of locally manufactured products. He said the Authority issued more than 1,200 certificates to Ghanaian products during the period under review, indicating that a significant number of the products tested met the required quality standards. “It is good news because last year we issued more than 1,200 certificates to Ghanaian products. This means that our products are meeting the quality mark.” He said the results demonstrated the importance of standards compliance in helping Ghanaian businesses access international markets. Prof. Agyei stressed, however, that maintaining the necessary laboratory capacity was essential to sustaining the certification regime and protecting Ghana’s access to global markets. For the GSA, resolving the procurement delays remains critical to ensuring that its laboratories have the equipment needed to verify the quality and safety of Ghanaian products, particularly those destined for export.

items.title: Witsel retires from internationals after 18-year Belgium career
items.description: Veteran midfielder Axel Witsel announced his retirement from international football on Wednesday, bringing an end to a Belgium career which saw him become their second-most capped player. The 37-year-old made his 140th and last appearance for the national side in their 2-1 World Cup quarter-final loss to eventual champions Spain in July. “It’s time to make way for the youngsters and the new generation,” Witsel said in a social media post. “I never imagined achieving so much when I started out at just 18 years old.” Witsel made his debut in 2008 and became a key player for Belgium’s ‘golden generation’, which also included Kevin De Bruyne, Romelu Lukaku and Eden Hazard. They never managed to win a major tournament, coming closest at the 2018 World Cup when they lost to France in the semi-finals. Only long-time teammate Jan Vertonghen, with 157 caps, has played more times for Belgium than Witsel. He joined Ligue 1 club Nice in the close-season from Girona, having previously played for Borussia Dortmund and Atletico Madrid. items.title: FIFA to review Infantino’s shelved World Cup investment plan
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA has confirmed that a review of the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) investment proposal will be presented to the FIFA Council, following criticism over the lack of answers surrounding the controversial plan. According to Reuters, the confirmation came after Danish Football Association president Jesper Moller criticised FIFA for failing to answer what he described as “critical questions” about the shelved proposal at a Legal Committee meeting. “FIFA Standing Committees advise and assist the FIFA Council in their respective fields in line with FIFA’s Statutes and Governance Regulations,” FIFA told Reuters in a statement. “As previously communicated, a review of the withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal will be presented to the FIFA Council.” The FIFA Council has 37 members, including president Gianni Infantino, eight vice-presidents and 28 members elected by FIFA’s member associations. The FFE proposal, launched by Infantino, sought to sell commercial stakes in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup, to outside investors. The plan triggered widespread opposition, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF among the football bodies calling for changes to FIFA’s leadership structure. The proposal was subsequently withdrawn following the backlash, while the fallout has continued to put pressure on Infantino ahead of the FIFA presidential election in March 2027. Several European football associations have since withdrawn their support for Infantino’s re-election bid, while Greek FA president Makis Gagatsis and former Germany national team director Oliver Bierhoff joined UEFA’s call for a leadership change on Tuesday. However, Reuters reported that people familiar with the discussions said Infantino retains sufficient backing to secure another term, prompting opponents to consider strategies focused on limiting his powers rather than defeating him at the ballot. The FIFA presidential election is scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat, with Infantino seeking a fourth term. Moller had previously criticised FIFA after the FFE proposal was not placed on the agenda of the Legal Committee meeting, saying the governing body had declined to provide answers to questions surrounding the project. The post FIFA to review Infantino’s shelved World Cup investment plan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bazèga/Ipelcé : La population mobilisée pour la destruction des gîtes larvaires
items.description: Burkina-Bazèga-Santé-Lutte-Paludisme Bazèga/Ipelcé : La population mobilisée pour la destruction des gîtes larvaires Ipelcé, 16 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Les populations de la commune de Ipelcé, dans la province du Bazèga, se sont mobilisées les 5 et 6 septembre 2026 pour une vaste opération d’assainissement visant notamment à détruire les gîtes larvaires, dans le cadre du deuxième passage de la Journée nationale de lutte anti-vectorielle (JNLAV). L’opération a réuni les appelés de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire, des associations de jeunes et de femmes, les services techniques déconcentrés ainsi que les autorités coutumières. Avec l’accompagnement de la société de carrière JOC-ER SA, neuf camions chargés de terre ont été mobilisés pour le remblayage des flaques d’eau, notamment au niveau du marché de Ipelcé et sur plusieurs autres sites de la commune. Munis de râteaux, pelles, balais et brouettes, les participants ont procédé au nettoyage du marché, au remblayage des flaques d’eau, au ramassage des pneus usagés et à l’arrachage des herbes susceptibles de favoriser la prolifération des moustiques. La présidente de la délégation spéciale (PDS), camarade N. Émeline Kiemtoré/Bonkoungou, a salué l’engagement des participants et invité les populations à maintenir leur cadre de vie propre et à poursuivre les actions d’assainissement au quotidien. Cette mobilisation s’inscrit dans les actions de prévention des maladies à transmission vectorielle, notamment le paludisme, à travers la réduction des gîtes larvaires. Agence d’information du Burkina DP/tpk/ap/ata

items.title: IERPP calls for withdrawal of proposed NPA Bill, raises concerns over BOST mandate
items.description: The Institute of Economic Research and Public Policy (IERPP) has called on the government and Parliament to withdraw the proposed National Petroleum Authority (NPA) Bill, warning that it could undermine the mandate of the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company (BOST) if passed in its current form. Executive Director of IERPP, Professor Isaac Boadi, said the proposed legislation could have implications for the management of Ghana’s strategic fuel reserves and the country’s broader fuel security. Speaking on the proposed bill, Prof. Boadi also raised concerns about what he described as inadequate consultation with key stakeholders before the legislation was introduced. “We’ve not had proper stakeholder consultation as far as this is concerned.” He urged the government and Parliament to withdraw the bill and subject it to further consultation and review. “We’re calling on government, Parliament to quickly withdraw the bill as early as possible and ensure we don’t pass the bill in its current state.” Concerns over BOST’s mandate Prof. Boadi argued that BOST plays an important role in Ghana’s fuel security by maintaining strategic storage capacity and serving as a source of supply during periods of disruption. He expressed concern that proposed changes under the bill could affect BOST’s existing mandate and, in turn, have implications for the country’s ability to manage strategic fuel reserves. He also raised concerns about the potential impact on jobs at BOST. According to Prof. Boadi, about 689 staff could be affected by the proposed changes, with him claiming that approximately half could potentially lose their jobs if the bill is passed in its current form. “If we allow it to be passed in its current form, about 50 percent of 689 staff will not have jobs anymore.” He linked the concern to the government’s 24 Hour Economy initiative, arguing that changes that potentially reduce employment at an existing institution would be difficult to reconcile with efforts to expand job opportunities. “We haven’t seen the result of the 24-hour economy yet if a bill in its current form [means] a lot of people will lose their jobs.” IERPP is therefore urging Parliament to subject the proposed legislation to further review and consultation, with particular attention to BOST’s mandate, employment implications and the management of Ghana’s strategic fuel reserves. The institute says any changes to the petroleum-sector regulatory framework should preserve Ghana’s fuel-security arrangements and ensure that critical national petroleum assets remain effectively managed.

items.title: CAN dismisses rumour of Alia’s plan to demolish Secretariat
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Benue State Chapter, has dismissed reports circulating on social media and other platforms alleging that Governor Hyacinth Alia was planning to demolish the association’s secretariat in the state. The Acting Chairman of CAN in the state, Rev. Jonathan Ugbede, described the report as false and malicious, insisting that the governor had never contemplated demolishing the secretariat. Ugbede, who spoke while reacting to the speculation, said the allegation was completely detached from reality and urged members of the Christian community in the state to disregard it. He expressed satisfaction with the governor’s prompt response to the allegation, noting that Alia had already debunked the report. According to him, the governor’s response was consistent with his administration’s relationship with the Church and other religious institutions in the state. A statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Solomon Iorpev, had quoted Alia as saying that he was a proud product of the Church and that his administration had consistently demonstrated respect, support and partnership with religious institutions across Benue State, including CAN. The governor, according to the statement, maintained that “no such plans, as falsely alleged, have been conceived, discussed or contemplated by the government.” Reacting, Ugbede appreciated Alia for his prompt clarification and appealed to politicians not to drag the Church into partisan politics. “I am happy that the governor has come out promptly to debunk the allegation. The publication is malicious, false, baseless and completely detached from the truth. “The political class should not drag the Church into the murky arena of politics. The Church belongs to everybody and should remain an institution that promotes peace, unity and the wellbeing of the people,” he said. The CAN leader further disclosed that Alia had continued to support activities of the association, including sponsoring some CAN programmes and assisting Christians with medical bills. He said the governor’s interventions had enabled some beneficiaries who were previously ill to recover and regain their strength. Ugbede questioned the motive behind the circulation of the alleged demolition report and urged those responsible for generating and spreading what he described as fake news to desist from actions capable of creating tension in the state. “What will be the benefit to the sponsors of such fake news and those spreading the news? Such fabrications can only create unnecessary tension and generate bad blood between the Church and the governor,” he said. The acting chairman urged Christians across Benue State not to panic over the report but to disregard the publication and its sponsors. He said the report was allegedly fabricated to create disunity and strain the relationship between the Church and the governor. Ugbede also called on members of the Christian community to intensify prayers for Alia and continue supporting his administration to enable it achieve more for the people of the state. He assured the governor that the Benue Church remained united and was not affected by the publication. “The Benue Church is solidly behind the governor. Our resolve to support him has remained unshaken,” Ugbede said. The post CAN dismisses rumour of Alia’s plan to demolish Secretariat appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Strike: JUSUN members disrupt activities at Nasarawa High Court
items.description: By Edwin Phillip, Lafia Members of the Judiciary Staff Union of Nigeria (JUSUN), Nasarawa State branch, on Wednesday staged a peaceful protest at the premises of the State High Court headquarters on Shadam Road, Lafia, in compliance with the indefinite strike declared by the union. Our correspondent reports that the union members carried placards with various inscriptions demanding, among other things, the implementation of salary increases and financial autonomy for the judiciary. Some of the placards read: “Let’s have our financial autonomy, time is now,” “Let’s have our right” and “Give us 40 percent increase in salary.” The main entrance of the court premises was, however, manned by a combined team of security personnel to prevent any breakdown of law and order. Addressing the protesters, the state Chairman of JUSUN, Comrade Mas’ud Ubangari, urged members to remain united, focused and law-abiding as they pressed for the implementation of their demands. Ubangari said the enforcement of the industrial action would be sustained peacefully until the state government and the Judicial Service Commission addressed the union’s demands. However, the Covering Director of Information and Protocol, Nasarawa State High Court of Justice, Mrs Esther Agube Ogidis, said the state Chief Judge had already put measures in place to address the demands of the judiciary staff. She questioned the decision to embark on the industrial action despite an order of the National Industrial Court restraining the union from proceeding with the strike. Similarly, the Director of Civil Litigation, Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Alhassan Sabo, described the industrial action as illegal. Sabo appealed to the JUSUN leadership to respect the interim injunction issued by the National Industrial Court restraining the union from commencing or declaring the strike pending the hearing and determination of the matter. The judiciary workers are demanding the implementation of a 58.1 per cent salary increase, financial autonomy for the judiciary and a 40 per cent peculiar allowance, among other demands. items.title: We’re not demolishing Konkomba Yam Market – Accra Mayor dismisses Minority’s claims
items.description: The Accra Mayor, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, has denied allegations that the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) is deliberately targeting the Konkomba community in plans to construct a 24-hour market at the site of the Konkomba Yam Market. The Mayor said the Assembly has engaged leaders of the Konkomba and other communities operating at the market ahead of the planned redevelopment. Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, Mr Allotey said he had personally visited the market several times and held meetings with traders before the project was initiated. “First of all, I want you to know that His Excellency John Dramani Mahama and the NDC party love Konkomba market and love Konkomba’s. We’ve been trying our best to better their lives,” he said. His comments follow accusations by the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Minority in Parliament that the AMA had marked virtually every shop and residential structure occupied by members of the Konkomba community for demolition while leaving other parts of the area untouched. The NPP Member of Parliament for Bimbilla and former Defence Minister Dominic Nitiwul, who led the Minority caucus to inspect the area, described the alleged targeting as discriminatory and called on President Mahama to stop the planned demolition. Mr Allotey, however, rejected the claims and said the AMA had engaged the affected communities. “I’ve been in the Konkomba market, I’ve gone there more than 15 times. Before we started this 24-hour market, I’ve been to the Konkomba market not one, not two, not three. I have been there, I have meetings with them,” he said. He said leaders of the Konkomba and Nzema communities had been engaged on the project, adding that some of the engagements had taken place at his office and the Ministry of Transport. “The leaders, the Konkomba people, the Nzema people, we have engaged them,” Mr Allotey said. He also dismissed claims by Mr Nitiwul that the Assembly had failed to engage the traders. “He lied from the beginning, because he said the mayor has not engaged the people,” he said. The Mayor stressed that the intention of the project was not to remove the Konkomba traders from the area but to improve their trading environment. “So we are not demolishing the Konkomba market,” he said. Mr Allotey said the Assembly’s commitment was to provide a better environment for the traders as part of the redevelopment. “But the promise we made to them was that we are going to better where they trade,” he said. He maintained that the planned 24-hour market formed part of efforts to improve conditions for traders and pledged that the project would be carried out in line with the government’s commitment to the community.

items.title: Suvie la Campagne agropastorale 2026-2027 : À Koupéla, le Ministre d’État Ismaël SOMBIÉ à l’écoute des attentes des producteurs et transformateurs
items.description: Dans le cadre de sa tournée de suivi de la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027, le Ministre d’État, Ministre de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le Camarade Commandant Ismaël SOMBIÉ, s’est rendu à Koupéla pour échanger directement avec les forces vives du monde rural de la province du Kouritenga. À travers des discussions franches et constructives avec l'ensemble des acteurs des différentes chaînes de valeur, cette rencontre visait à recenser les difficultés du terrain et à véhiculer la vision du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, pour la souveraineté alimentaire et la résilience du monde rural burkinabè. À Koupéla, chef-lieu de la province du Kouritenga dans la région du Nakambé, la tournée de suivi de la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027 a donné lieu à une grande immersion auprès des acteurs du monde rural. Éleveurs, maraîchers, producteurs de céréales, pisciculteurs, aviculteurs, transformateurs et ferrailleurs se sont réunis autour du Ministre d’État, le Camarade Commandant Ismaël SOMBIÉ, pour exposer leurs réalités quotidiennes. Au-delà du recensement des contraintes, la rencontre a permis de transmettre le message du Camarade Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, axé sur la productivité, la résilience et l'autonomie alimentaire du Burkina Faso. La maîtrise de l'eau et la préservation des espaces exploitables se sont affirmées comme des préoccupations majeures partagées par l'ensemble des filières. Les maraîchers et les producteurs de cultures vivrières (riz, maïs, blé, arachide, manioc) ont vivement plaidé pour la réalisation de forages à gros débit, la réhabilitation des plaines aménagées et le curage des barrages existants. Pour pérenniser ces infrastructures d'eau, les usagers ont insisté sur la nécessité de protéger les retenues contre les activités dégradantes. Sur le plan foncier, la délimitation urgente de la plaine de Itengué face à la pression de l'extension urbaine a été particulièrement mise en avant par les exploitants. Sur le plan de la production brute, les besoins logistiques et techniques restent nombreux. Bien que les producteurs semenciers aient salué le soutien de l'État pour l'enlèvement annuel de 20 000 tonnes de semences, ils ont réclamé un renforcement des équipements lourds — tels que des motoculteurs et des batteuses-vaneuses — ainsi que l'accroissement des capacités de stockage. Côté élevage et production laitière, les acteurs ont sollicité un appui accru en aliments pour bétail, le développement d'espaces d’embouche et le renforcement des points d'eau pastoraux. Dans le secteur avicole, l'accès à des couvoirs régionaux et la proximité des aliments produits par Faso Guulgo demeurent prioritaires. Pour la filière arachide, l'accent a été mis sur la lutte contre l'aflatoxine et les pesticides non homologués. La transformation et la commercialisation des produits locaux représentent le dernier maillon essentiel pour accroître la valeur ajoutée régionale. Les transformateurs de maïs, riz, arachide, attiéké, tout comme les acteurs des produits forestiers non ligneux (miel, karité, soumbala), ont proposé l'intégration systématique des produits locaux dans l'approvisionnement des cantines scolaires. Ils ont également souligné la nécessité d'alléger le coût de certification des produits, d'acquérir du matériel de transformation en inox et d'accéder à des formations spécialisées en marketing et vente en ligne. Ces remontées de terrain directes serviront désormais de boussole aux interventions publiques pour mieux ajuster le soutien de l'État aux besoins réels du monde rural. L’article Suvie la Campagne agropastorale 2026-2027 : À Koupéla, le Ministre d’État Ismaël SOMBIÉ à l’écoute des attentes des producteurs et transformateurs est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Petroleum dealers demand govt devise mechanism for fuel subsidy reimbursement
items.description: KARACHI: Petroleum dealers have called on the government to devise a mechanism for reimbursing the fuel subsidy, which is set to take effect across the country from midnight on Wednesday. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Under the scheme, a relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres will be provided to bike and auto owners, while those owning small vehicles of up to 800cc will get a relief of Rs100 per litre for a monthly quota of 30 litres. “We welcome the government’s move for the benefit of the public, but our businesses should not suffer,” Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) Chairman Malik Khuda Bakhsh said. He was addressing an emergency press conference on Wednesday along with other office-bearers of the association. “The fuel subsidy scheme started in Islamabad at midnight on Tuesday and will be launched across the country from tonight,” Malik said. He added: “But our issue is that petroleum dealers are asking us: who will pay the subsidy amount and when?” He explained that no fuel station could afford to bear a loss of Rs100 per litre or wait for delayed payments for a long period. “We have approached the Petroleum Division, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) and even the Finance Ministry to get an answer to one simple question,” Khuda Bakhsh said. He added that the confusion was compounded by the fact that it appeared none of the authorities themselves were aware of the issue. “The officials of Ogra and oil marketing companies say that the Petroleum Division will possibly pay the subsidy amount, whereas Petroleum Division officials maintain that the payments will be made by the Finance Ministry. A Finance Ministry official has assured us that the State Bank will release the funds within a day or two,” he added. He also maintained that the federal government had assured the dealers that they would be taken into confidence before the launch of the fuel relief package. “The government has to understand that if payments are not reimbursed on time, many dealers will stop participating in the scheme, as many previous promises made by the government were not fulfilled,” he added. PPDA Vice Chairman Tariq Hassan said that around 14,000 dealers across the country had been trying to contact the government for the past three days, but whenever the government wanted to enforce something, it stopped communication. Another vice chairman, Anwar Kamal, said that if the scheme was to be successful, the government must negotiate with dealers. He also rejected the government’s proposed “smart lockdown”. He added that billions of rupees belonging to dealers should not remain tied up for a long period under the scheme. Meanwhile, Minister Shaza Fatima announced on Wednesday night that the issue related to the forwarding of SMS messages from preloaded packages and low balances had been resolved. “The prime minister has made the SMS for the fuel subsidy available free of charge, and Jazz has completed the system shift. Other telecom companies will also do so by Thursday,” she added.

items.title: TPI Mafanco : TPI de Mafanco : 5 ans d’interdiction de conduire pour un motard impliqué dans la mort d’un gendarme
items.description: Poursuivi pour homicide involontaire après avoir mortellement percuté un gendarme à Gbessia, Malal Doumbouya, 20 ans, a été condamné ce mercredi 16 septembre 2026 à deux ans de prison avec sursis, un million de francs guinéens d’amende et cinq ans d’interdiction de conduire une moto. L’accident s’est produit le 9 septembre dernier, sous le pont de Gbessia. D’après les débats à l’audience, le jeune motard circulait à vive allure lorsqu’une collision avec un autre motocycliste est survenue. Un gendarme qui traversait la chaussée a été percuté dans la foulée. À la barre du tribunal correctionnel de Mafanco, présidé par le juge Mohamed Lamine Cissé, le prévenu n’a pas contesté les faits. « Je partais à la maison. Je suis entré en collision avec un autre motard sous le pont de Gbessia et c’est ainsi que la victime, qui traversait, a été percutée », a-t-il expliqué, avant d’exprimer ses regrets et de demander pardon. Le parquet a indiqué que les constatations faisaient ressortir un excès de vitesse. La moto conduite par le prévenu n’était également pas immatriculée. Grièvement touché dans l’accident, le gendarme a été projeté à environ deux mètres du point d’impact. Il a été transporté à l’hôpital, mais a succombé à ses blessures deux jours plus tard. Dans son réquisitoire, le ministère public a cependant souligné que la victime traversait à un endroit qui n’était pas prévu à cet effet. Le procureur a notamment rappelé les risques liés à la traversée des autoroutes et des axes à forte circulation en dehors des passerelles aménagées. Tout en retenant l’excès de vitesse à l’encontre du prévenu, le parquet a demandé au tribunal de tenir compte de plusieurs circonstances, notamment son jeune âge, son activité génératrice de revenus et la position des parents de la victime, qui auraient plaidé en faveur de sa libération. « En réalité c'est par le faits de la victime que l'accident est survenu. Dès lors qu'elle traversait sur un endroit non reglementé avec des airpods. Les faits sont donc survenus par la négligence de la victime.Tout ce qu'on peut reprocher au conducteur, c'est l'excès de vitesse « . Le ministère public a ainsi requis un an de prison avec sursis, cinq millions de francs guinéens d’amende et une interdiction de conduire une moto pendant au moins un an. Après avoir une dernière fois sollicité la clémence du tribunal, Malal Doumbouya a été déclaré coupable d’homicide involontaire. Le tribunal lui a finalement infligé deux ans de prison avec sursis, un million de francs guinéens d’amende et cinq ans d’interdiction de conduire une moto.

items.title: Scandale foncier à Koumassi : Vers la levée de l’immunité d’un député, le parquet démonte la thèse de la décision de justice et réclame la vérité
items.description: Plus de trois mois après la destruction controversée de logements au quartier Campement dans la commune de Koumassi, le Procureur de la République près le Tribunal de Première Instance du Plateau, Braman Koné, a fait le point sur l'enquête judiciaire lors d'une conférence de presse. Qualifiant les démolitions survenues le 3 juin 2026 d'illégales, le parquet met en lumière des décisions de justice dévoyées, l'implication du ministre-gouverneur Cissé Ibrahima Bacongo et la demande de levée d'immunité d'un député soupçonné d'avoir financé l'opération. Le mercredi 16 septembre 2026, la salle des pas perdus du Tribunal de Première Instance du Plateau à Abidjan a servi de cadre à une communication très attendue du Procureur de la République, Braman Koné. L'objectif principal de cette intervention était de présenter l'état d'avancement de l'information judiciaire ouverte le 10 juin 2026, à la suite des destructions ayant secoué le quartier Campement de Koumassi. Dès ses propos liminaires, le procureur a fermement établi que la démolition de maisons effectuée le 3 juin 2026 s'était déroulée dans un cadre strictement illégal. Détournement de décision judiciaire et mandat de dépôt Alors que le nommé Alloui Brou Jacques affirmait publiquement sur les réseaux sociaux agir en vertu d'un titre de justice, les vérifications menées par les enquêteurs ont démontré une tout autre réalité. La décision invoquée n'autorisait en aucun cas la destruction de constructions ; les juges n'avaient en effet ordonné que le déguerpissement de cinq habitations bien précises, sans jamais prescrire de démolition. À la suite de ces constats, une information judiciaire a été ouverte à l'encontre d'Alloui Brou Jacques le 29 juin 2026, suivie de l'émission d'un mandat de dépôt et de la tenue d'auditions. Le plan ORSEC au cœur des interrogations et audition d'un ministre-gouverneur L'affaire implique également d'importantes personnalités administratives. Entendu le 24 juin 2026 par le Premier président de la Cour d'appel d'Abidjan, le ministre-gouverneur Cissé Ibrahima Bacongo a justifié l'opération ordonnée par ses services en invoquant le plan d'urgence ORSEC. Si son directeur de cabinet admet avoir supervisé l'intervention sur ses instructions et que son directeur technique confirme la présence des forces policières sur les lieux, le parquet cherche désormais à déterminer si ce plan d'urgence s'appliquait légalement à cette situation précise et à établir l'ensemble des responsabilités. Soupçons sur un député, aveux forcés et imbroglio foncier L'enquête s'oriente par ailleurs vers le député de Gouméré-Tabagne, soupçonné d'avoir coordonné et principalement financé l'opération, notamment par le biais d'un prêt de 7 millions de francs CFA contracté en 2024 au profit d'Alloui Brou Jacques. Selon les déclarations du fils aîné d'Alloui Brou Jacques, l’élu aurait même exigé de son père qu'il s'accuse publiquement des démolitions dans une vidéo enregistrée. Face à ces éléments, la doyenne des juges d'instruction a demandé au procureur général de solliciter l'Assemblée nationale afin de lever l'immunité parlementaire du député pour d'éventuelles poursuites. Sur le plan cadastral, le site de plus de 6 hectares divisé en 250 lots révèle un statut juridique très complexe, mêlant arrêtés de concession définitive, titres fonciers au nom de l'État et démarches de morcellement. Face à ces enjeux, Braman Koné a réitéré la détermination du parquet à faire appliquer la loi en toute impartialité. L’article Scandale foncier à Koumassi : Vers la levée de l'immunité d'un député, le parquet démonte la thèse de la décision de justice et réclame la vérité est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.description: Mémorandum d’entente entre l’UNA et l’ICAIRE pour atteindre des objectifs communs RIYAD (UNA) – L’Union des agences de presse des États membres de l’Organisation de la coopération islamique (UNA) a signé aujourd’hui, mercredi 16 septembre 2026 à Riyad, un mémorandum d’entente avec le Centre international de recherche et d’éthique de l’intelligence artificielle (ICAIRE), en marge des travaux du quatrième Forum mondial de l’UNESCO sur l’éthique de l’intelligence artificielle (GFEAI 2026), qui a débuté le 14 septembre et prendra fin demain, 17 septembre. Mohammed bin Abd Rabbo Al-Yami, Directeur général de l’UNA, et au nom de l’ICAIRE par Son Excellence Dr Majed bin Ali Al-Shehri, Directeur général de l’ICAIRE. Ce mémorandum vise à concrétiser les objectifs communs de l’ICAIRE, dont les axes s’inscrivent dans le cadre de la Stratégie à moyen terme de l’UNESCO (2022–2029), ainsi que ceux de l’UNA, qui sont en adéquation avec les objectifs stratégiques de l’UNESCO en matière de promotion de la liberté d’expression et du développement des médias, de diffusion d’une culture de paix et de tolérance, de lutte contre les discours de haine et l’extrémisme, de soutien à l’échange des connaissances et au renforcement des capacités médiatiques à l’ère numérique, de coordination des programmes de formation destinés aux professionnels des médias, de promotion d’une transformation technologique éthique et de développement de partenariats en vue d’un impact durable. items.title: Attaque au drone contre La Mecque : l’Algérie réagit
items.description: L’Algérie a réagi ce mercredi à l’attaque au drone qui a ciblé mardi La Mecque en dénonçant une « agression extrêmement dangereuse » contre les lieux saints de l’islam. Dans un communiqué du ministère des Affaires étrangères, l’Algérie a « condamné fermement » le ciblage de la ville sainte de La Mecque en Arabie saoudite par un drone hostile, qu’elle considère comme une « agression extrêmement dangereuse contre les lieux saints des musulmans du monde entier ». L’Algérie a dénoncé une « provocation flagrante à l’égard de leurs sentiments et une violation manifeste du caractère sacré de la Mosquée sacrée ». L’Algérie dénonce les « attaques odieuses » contre l’Arabie saoudite Face à ces « attaques odieuses », l’Algérie a réaffirmé son « plein soutien à l’Arabie saoudite dans la protection des lieux saints des musulmans et de l’ensemble de son territoire » et son soutien à « toutes les mesures que le Royaume jugera appropriées pour garantir sa sécurité et sa stabilité et préserver sa souveraineté nationale ». Dans le même communiqué, l’Algérie a renouvelé son « appel à la cessation immédiate de ces attaques et de toute forme d’escalade et de provocation dans la région, qui ne font qu’aggraver la situation et l’exposer à des conséquences dangereuses et imprévisibles ». Mardi, l’Arabie saoudite a annoncé avoir intercepté et détruit un drone hostile au-dessus de La Mecque et accusé les Houthis d’avoir perpétré cette attaque, la première du genre dans l’histoire de la ville qui abrite des lieux saints de l’islam. items.title: Nitiwul, Accra Mayor clash over Konkomba Yam Market demolition for 24-Hour-Economy market
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Bimbilla Dominic Nitiwul and Accra Mayor Michael Kpakpo Allotey have clashed over plans to demolish parts of the Konkomba Yam Market at Agbogbloshie to make way for a proposed 24-hour economy market. Mr Nitiwul has questioned what he believes is the concentration on the section of the market occupied predominantly by Konkomba traders, while other parts of the market are reportedly not affected. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story, Mr Allotey rejected the suggestion that the Konkomba community was being singled out. He said he had visited the market more than 15 times before the 24-hour market project was introduced and was involved in marking the area earmarked for redevelopment. The mayor also challenged Mr Nitiwul’s account of the consultation process, accusing him of misleading the public about the project. “I don’t sit in the office, I am not an office mayor, I don’t wear political suit. I am always on the ground, I know what I am about, I know what I am saying, I don’t give fake news, I don’t deceive people,” he said on Wednesday, September 16. Mr Allotey said the administration of President John Dramani Mahama had been seeking to improve conditions for Konkomba traders and insisted that the community was not being targeted. Mr Nitiwul, however, maintained that his concerns were about protecting the interests of traders and yam producers connected to the market. He said millions of people rely on the Konkomba Yam Market and that a significant proportion of yam producers in his constituency supply the market. “In the case of the kokomba market, my people are the people of Ghana, the million people who buy yam at the kokomba yam market. 3-4 million yam are sold daily at the konkomba yam market so I represent those people. I also represent the yam producers from my own constituency, 90% of the yam producers are from my constituency so I represent them and I speak for them.” A key point of disagreement is the engagement between the Accra Metropolitan Assembly and the market’s leadership. Mr Nitiwul said the mayor met leaders of the Konkomba Yam Market on July 28 and presented them with markings and drawings showing the proposed development. He said the traders told the mayor that it was their first meeting with them and that previous engagements had involved people they did not regard as their representatives. Mr Allotey disputed the account and accused the MP of contradicting earlier statements about whether consultations had taken place. “You lied to the people. I have not met them as at that time, you told them we just woke up and we decided to do this work. You lied to the people and you have to apologise.”

items.title: Le Comité d’organisation de la «Nuit de la Révolution» reçoit les orientations du Premier ministre
items.description: AN 4 DE LA RÉVOLUTION PROGRESSISTE POPULAIRE (RPP) Le Comité d’organisation de la «Nuit de la Révolution» reçoit les orientations du Premier ministre (Ouagadougou, 16 septembre 2026). Le Premier ministre, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel OUÉDRAOGO a accordé, ce mercredi dans la matinée, une audience à une délégation du Comité d’organisation de la Nuit de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP), un évènement majeur qui va clôturer les actions de communication de l’AN4 de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire. Conduite par le Ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Porte-parole du Gouvernement, le Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO, la délégation est allée faire le point du plan d’actions au Chef du Gouvernement, et recueillir ses orientations pour mieux affiner l’organisation de cette Nuit qui entend créer un rassemblement populaire autour des acquis et de la vision de la RPP. « Nous avons retenu de célébrer en apothéose du mois anniversaire, la Nuit de la Revolution Progressiste Populaire, le 30 septembre prochain. Ce sera un moment de communion populaire et nous voulons y inviter l’ensemble des Burkinabè partout où ils se trouvent », a indiqué le Camarade Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO. Il a soutenu que cet évènement se veut une occasion pour célébrer les victoires, réaffirmer notre attachement à la souveraineté et expliquer les idéaux de la RPP. Selon le Ministre en charge de la Communication, cet évènement se tiendra à la Place de la Révolution à Ouagadougou, dans les chefs-lieux de région et dans les représentations diplomatiques de notre pays à l’étranger. « Nous voulons que partout où il y a des Burkinabè, partout où il y a des Africains qui croient à l’idéal révolutionnaire porté par le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, que les amis du Burkina Faso se mettent ensemble, pour qu’en bons veilleurs et gardiens de la Révolution, nous puissions prendre part à cette Nuit qui va se dérouler de 18h à 2h du matin », a souligné le Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO. Au cours de cette Nuit de la RPP, il y aura également des prestations d’artistes nationaux, des artistes internationaux et des fenêtres pour montrer des actions concrètes, des acquis de la RPP sous le leadership du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. Réussir le défi de la mobilisation Dans cette perspective, tout en encourageant le Comité d’organisation, le Camarade Premier ministre a insisté sur la nécessité de relever le défi de la mobilisation par la communication et l’implication des autorités administratives au niveau des régions autour de cet évènement national majeur. Selon le Camarade Premier ministre, cette Nuit doit être un moment d’exaltation, un tremplin pour montrer au Peuple burkinabè les résultats de son sursaut avec le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. Pour ce faire, il a donné instruction au Comité de travailler « à ce que la mobilisation soit importante parce que nous ne voulons pas qu’un seul Burkinabè soit laissé en marge », a souligné le Camarade Gilbert Pingdwendé OUÉDRAOGO. items.title: Pakistan to stand by Saudi Arabia 'practically and diplomatically' if Yemen conflict escalates: Asif
items.description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Wednesday said Pakistan would “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalated. Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen’s Houthis accused the rebels of targeting the holy city of Makkah, sparking outrage across the Muslim world and deepening the conflict roiling the region. However, the Houthis swiftly rejected Riyadh’s report as a “lie” that it shot down a drone from the rebels heading towards Makkah. “If the situation escalates, we will stand with Saudi Arabia, both practically and diplomatically,” he said while speaking on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shehzaib Khanzada Ke Saath’. Commenting on the Pakistan-Turkiye-Saudi Arabia trilateral agreement — the Makkah Defence Alliance — he affirmed that an agreement was in place. However, he said that even if there had been no such agreement, Pakistan was bound by an “eternal agreement to respond if the holy sites come under attack”. “There are some worldly agreements, too, and they have their own sanctity and obligations, but protecting the holy sites is our religious duty,” he said. Asif maintained that Muslims around the world did not need an agreement to act if the holy sites in Makkah or Medina came under attack. “There is no need to activate any agreement,” he said. The defence minister maintained that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries. “There is absolutely no ambiguity,” he asserted. Asked about any military or political engagement with the Houthis, Asif said he could not disclose details, adding that strategies at this level were not meant to be made public. However, he reiterated that Pakistan was bound by the agreement. “Under the trilateral agreement, if the territorial integrity of a country comes under threat, the agreement will be activated and the other two countries will proceed to protect it in fulfilment of their obligations,” he said. “The situation has arrived.” On the US-Israeli war on Iran, Asif said it had become clear, a month into the conflict, that Israel’s calculations had not produced the expected results. “Israel sucked America into this war as a combatant party, but under the present circumstances, the world and the region need to realise that Israel is the real culprit,” he said. “Until Israel is confronted by a joint alliance, it will remain a threat to the region. The Zionist lobby also forces the US to join Israel’s wars.” Sharing his personal view on possible Iranian support for the Houthis, he said Iran, as a state, might not be backing the group as it was already embroiled in another conflict in the Middle East. “This would be a diplomatic error if Iran were to take the side of the Houthis, but the chances are minimal. Escalating the conflict into another theatre is not a wise decision and could turn it into a wider conflict,” Asif said. Fresh fighting between the Houthis and the Yemeni government has dragged in Riyadh, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. Last week’s lightning offensive saw the group seize control of the entirety of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital artery for Saudi oil exports as the wider Middle East war chokes off the Strait of Hormuz strategic shipping route. Pakistan’s stance Earlier today, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that the defence alliance has no “regional aspirations”, adding that it is intended for collective deterrence . The military spokesperson made the remarks during an interview on Al Arabiya English ’s programme ‘Global News Today’, during a conversation with the host, Tom Burges Watson. “It formalises Pakistan’s decades-old relationship with the kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the brotherly country of Turkiye in the domains of collective deterrence and defence,” he said. Watson asked whether the pact was primarily a defensive cooperation or the beginning of a broader strategic alliance. To that, Lt Gen Chaudhry asserted that the pact was defensive, as its name implied. “It is defensive. There’s nothing aggressive. There are no regional aspirations. It is collective deterrence,” he said, adding that the agreement was also “complementary”. During the interview, Lt Gen Chaudhry was also asked whether he saw the defence agreement becoming a part of the wider, Muslim-world security architecture. He replied that there was nothing in the pact that stated that it was a Muslim alliance, adding that it was an alliance for regional stability. “It is not a club that is being made for only Muslim countries,” he said, adding that decisions on its expansion were to be taken by the leadership of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. “This agreement, this alliance can always encompass new, willing partners who also believe in regional peace, stability and security, [and] who have a shared vision of non-aggression, non-interference and collective deterrence. “But that’s for the leadership of these three countries to decide; the how and when part,” he elaborated. The joint defence pact was signed on Aug 7 and provides that an attack on one member state would be treated as an attack on all. Its inaugural meeting was held in Istanbul on Aug 31, where it was decided that Pakistan would initially head the alliance’s secretariat for three years. Since its signing, there has been conversation about the possibility of its expansion, with Turkiye initially suggesting the possibility of Egypt’s inclusion. Though there has been no confirmation from Cairo. From Pakistan, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar clarified soon after the signing that the pact was defensive in nature, with the latter saying that it was also “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles. However, when Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjah Haider Khan was asked about possibility of the pact’s expansion during a weekly media briefing last week, he said an expansion was not on the cards at that point. The three countries first needed to solidify the new organisation before considering opening it to other states with similar threat perceptions and requirements, he explained.

items.title: Sécurisation des titres académiques : Le Burkina Faso fait le pari de la biométrie lors de la 7ᵉ édition de l’ID DAY
items.description: La 7ᵉ édition de la Journée internationale de l’identité (ID DAY 2026) s’est tenue ce mercredi 16 septembre 2026 à l’Université Joseph KI-ZERBO, sous la présidence du Ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou SANA, et en présence du Ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, le Camarade Pr Adjima THOMBIONO. Axée sur l’intégration de l’identification de base et de la biométrie dans la sécurisation des diplômes académiques et professionnels, cette célébration s'inscrit au cœur de la refondation de l'État et vise à bâtir un pont stratégique entre l'état civil et le parcours académique des citoyens. Ce mercredi 16 septembre 2026, le campus de l’Université Joseph KI-ZERBO a abrité les cérémonies et travaux de la 7ᵉ édition de la Journée internationale de l’identité (ID DAY 2026). Placé sous la présidence du Camarade Mahamadou SANA, Ministre de la Sécurité, l'événement s'est déroulé aux côtés du Camarade Pr Adjima THOMBIONO, Ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation. Cette célébration conjointe s'insère directement « au cœur du vaste processus de refondation et de transformation de notre État », traduisant une volonté politique d'interconnecter la sécurité identitaire et l'appareil éducatif national. Un pont stratégique entre l’état civil, la biométrie et les diplômes Le thème central retenu pour cette édition, « Intégration de l’identification de base et de la biométrie dans la gestion et la sécurisation des diplômes académiques et professionnels », pose les bases d'une réforme de fond. L'objectif affiché par le gouvernement consiste à relier l’identité de base du citoyen — authentifiée et sécurisée par les services de l'État — aux parchemins et titres délivrés par les universités et les centres de formation professionnelle. Comme l'a explicité le Ministre Mahamadou SANA, il s'agit d'une orientation stratégique majeure destinée à créer « un pont stratégique entre l’état civil, la biométrie et le parcours académique de chaque Burkinabè ». Consolider la confiance dans les documents officiels et l'action publique Réunissant un panel diversifié d'acteurs de l'identification, de la biométrie, de la certification et de la transformation numérique, l'ID DAY 2026 offre un cadre de concertation sur la modernisation des services publics. Les échanges engagés visent à mettre en lumière l'urgence de poursuivre les réformes technologiques et réglementaires du système d'état civil. En garantissant une traçabilité rigoureuse et une fiabilité accrue dans les mécanismes de délivrance des diplômes, les autorités ambitionnent d'éradiquer la fraude documentaire et de consolider durablement la confiance des citoyens et des partenaires dans les actes officiels et l'action de l'État. L’article Sécurisation des titres académiques : Le Burkina Faso fait le pari de la biométrie lors de la 7ᵉ édition de l'ID DAY est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: BoG urges digital asset businesses to build compliance into operations at Digital Assets Summit Africa
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) is urging digital asset businesses to make regulatory compliance an integral part of their operations from the outset, rather than waiting for regulators to intervene. Head of Fintech and Innovation at the Bank of Ghana, Elhanan Owureku Asare, who spoke on behalf of the Governor at the second edition of the Digital Assets Summit Africa, said businesses must prioritise transparency, responsible marketing and the protection of customers’ assets. He said the rapid development of digital assets presents regulatory and consumer protection questions that require close collaboration between industry players and regulators. “Digital assets are prompting many of the same questions that emerged when digital payments first began expanding rapidly. Could regulators keep pace? Would consumers be adequately protected? How would risk be managed?” Mr Asare said businesses must therefore take responsibility for ensuring that their operations meet the required regulatory standards as the sector develops. The comments come as Ghana continues to strengthen its regulatory framework for virtual assets, following the passage of the Virtual Assets Providers Bill in December last year. Chief Executive Officer of Promark Elite Limited, Peter Fempomanson, organisers of the Digital Assets Summit Africa, said the passage of the legislation represents one of the key developments between last year’s summit and this year’s edition. “Last year, when I was fortunate to be with you, there was nothing like the Virtual Assets Providers Bill. So you may recall that in September, we had the Digital Assets Summit Africa, and we had a huge representation from Bank of Ghana as well as Securities and Exchange Commission.” According to him, the engagement between industry stakeholders and regulators has helped to sustain discussions around the development and regulation of the digital asset sector. “We take a great deal of pride in that because we felt that the conversation that we started on the sidelines some few years ago is now gaining the necessary momentum, and the Bank of Ghana and Securities and Exchange Commission, who are the key regulators in this space, have taken the conversation seriously.” Mr Frimpong-Manso also said the second edition of the summit has attracted significant interest, with organisers having to close registration ahead of the event because of the high number of participants. “You see the number of people who have gathered here this morning, we are basically overwhelmed. And at some point yesterday, I was fortunate to be in your studio, and we had to close the registration.” Beyond discussions on digital assets and regulation, he said the summit is also focused on creating opportunities for startups and small businesses with innovative ideas but limited access to capital Mr Frimpong Manso said the initiative forms part of the organisers’ broader effort to ensure that the summit translates into practical opportunities for businesses and entrepreneurs beyond the digital assets conversation.

items.title: NGIS Money Market Fund’s net assets rise 33.3% to GH¢11.78m
items.description: The NGIS Money Market Fund PLC recorded strong growth in 2025, increasing its net assets by 33.3% from GH¢8.84 million in 2024 to GH¢11.78 million, despite a significant decline in interest rates during the year. The performance was announced at the 21st Annual General Meeting. Board Chairman of the Fund, Prof. Kwaku Dwumor Kessey, attributed the performance to the resilience of the Fund’s investment strategy and growing investor confidence. The Fund’s Net Asset Value per Share (NAVPS) increased from GH¢1.2319 to GH¢1.3778, representing an 11.84% growth, while total investment income rose by 13.4%, from GH¢1.44 million to GH¢1.63 million. Investor participation also strengthened, with proceeds from the issue of shares rising by 76.4%, from GH¢3.43 million in 2024 to GH¢6.06 million in 2025. Although withdrawals increased as investors used the Fund for liquidity management, subscriptions continued to exceed redemptions, generating net capital inflows of GH¢2.94 million, compared with GH¢2.22 million in 2024. Prof. Kessey said the results were achieved against the backdrop of a major shift in Ghana’s interest-rate environment, which saw yields on Treasury bills and other short-term fixed-income instruments decline considerably. “The decline in interest rates, while positive for the broader economy, presented a different challenge for money market investors. Yields on Treasury bills and other short-term fixed-income instruments declined considerably during the year”, he said. He said the Fund Manager therefore had to continuously reassess the portfolio to identify opportunities capable of delivering competitive returns without compromising the Fund’s objectives of capital preservation and liquidity. Prof. Kessey also encouraged individuals to put their money to work rather than keeping it idle. “Don’t keep your money in your house,it will not give you anything, but if you invest no matter how small the investment is, since the economy is growing your money will be growing with the economy, and you’ll have the benefit of growth,” he noted. On the outlook for 2026, Prof. Kessey said Ghana’s economic prospects were considerably more encouraging than at the beginning of 2025, citing moderating inflation, improved exchange-rate stability and strengthening economic activity. He, however, acknowledged the Fund’s exposure to wider economic risks, citing the restructuring of cocoa bills as an example. “We bought Cocoa bills which the Cocoa marketing board bought to purchase Cocoa and that was just for six months, we were going to get our money back plus the interest and this financial crisis came and they said that the bills have now been turned into bonds. So instead of six months, they’re going to pay us after five years which is a risk we took,” he noted. Chief Executive Officer of New Generation Investment Services Limited, Mr Edward K. Asamoah, said exceptionally high yields recorded in previous years might not return soon under the lower interest-rate environment. He noted, however, that lower inflation could improve investors’ real purchasing power and create a more stable investment environment. Mr Asamoah said the Fund Manager would focus on actively managing maturities and reinvestment risks, identifying opportunities across the yield curve, maintaining strong liquidity buffers, and carefully managing credit and counterparty risks.

items.title: I dare anyone with evidence against me to speak up — Jarvis
items.description: …says campaign should be issue-based, not personal attacks By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Cross River State, Sir Arthur Jarvis Archibong, has challenged anyone with evidence of criminal wrongdoing against him to make it public. Archibong, who spoke with journalists in Calabar on Wednesday, was reacting to a recent advertorial which he alleged was linked to the state government and intended to damage his reputation ahead of the 2027 governorship election. He said his campaign would remain focused on issues and development rather than personal attacks. “I dare anyone with criminal records against me to make same public or forever remain silent. “I am an honest, clean, and hardworking citizen of Cross River State in particular and Nigeria at large. “I have no criminal records on any matter, anywhere in Nigeria,” he said. Archibong alleged that the advertorial was an attempt to undermine his political standing across the state’s three senatorial districts. He also criticised the state government’s performance, alleging shortcomings in infrastructure and human development. The PDP candidate further alleged that the advertorial contained accusations against the administration relating to cultism and syncretism. He also alleged that there was a plan to deploy cult groups to cause violence before, during and after the 2027 elections. “We are aware that this government is planning unprecedented violence through cultism before, during, and after elections, but we are not afraid because God is our shield and buckler,” he said. Insisting that his campaign remained anchored on issues rather than personal attacks, Archibong accused the government and its supporters of engaging in what he described as personality-driven politics. He added that any response from his camp would be in reaction to what he considered provocations from the administration. Reacting to the allegations, the All Progressives Congress (APC) dismissed Archibong’s claim of a planned deployment of cult groups for electoral violence as baseless. The party’s state Publicity Secretary, Emmanuel Inyang, said Cross River residents had remained supportive of the APC because of what he described as the administration’s achievements in the state over the past three years. Inyang described Archibong’s allegations as the position of a party that was not prepared to face the electorate, and urged the PDP to prepare for the 2027 election. He said the PDP should get ready to face what he described as defeat at the polls. The post I dare anyone with evidence against me to speak up — Jarvis appeared first on Vanguard News .

L’inspecteur de l’enseignement primaire de la circonscription de Niaogho, Ousmane Compaoré, a effectué des visites dans plusieurs écoles pour s’assurer de la reprise effective des activités administratives. Selon lui, les onze écoles visitées ont toutes enregistré une reprise effective des activités administratives. Au cours des échanges avec le personnel enseignant, Ousmane Compaoré a salué l’engagement et le dévouement des acteurs de l’éducation. Il les félicite pour leur sens du devoir envers la nation et les exhorte à faire preuve de courage et de persévérance afin d’assurer un encadrement de qualité aux apprenants. Les acteurs éducatifs entendent ainsi conjuguer engagement et disponibilité des outils pédagogiques pour réussir cette nouvelle année scolaire. Agence d’Information du Burkina AA/SM/rbk/ata

items.title: Trafic d’explosifs et marchandises clandestines : La CNLF frappe fort avec la saisie de plus de 86 millions de FCFA de produits frauduleux
items.description: En moins d’un mois d'opérations intensives menées sur plusieurs axes routiers et marchés stratégiques, la Coordination Nationale de Lutte contre la Fraude (CNLF) a intercepté des marchandises illicites d'une valeur totale de plus de 86,4 millions de FCFA. Entre la saisie inédite de plus de 2 000 bâtons d'explosifs dissimulés dans des sacs d'engrais et l'interception de cargaisons de cigarettes, de boissons et de produits pour chicha, la CNLF démontre que la traque de la contrebande se trouve désormais au cœur des enjeux de sécurité nationale. L’alerte est maximale et la riposte de la Coordination Nationale de Lutte contre la Fraude (CNLF) s'intensifie sur le terrain. Le 5 septembre dernier, lors d'une intervention ciblée menée aux abords du marché Sankar Yarr, les équipes de contrôle ont fait une découverte troublante : 2 046 bâtons d’explosifs et 32 rouleaux de cordons détonants soigneusement cachés au milieu de simples sacs d’engrais. Évalué à 10,6 millions de FCFA, ce matériel mortel destiné aux circuits clandestins revêt une importance cruciale dans le contexte sécuritaire national actuel. Un coup d'arrêt aux cargaisons de cigarettes, boissons et chicha Cette intervention spectaculaire s'inscrit dans une offensive plus vaste déployée entre le 24 août et le 10 septembre. Les agents de la CNLF ont multiplié les opérations sur des points névralgiques, notamment sur l’axe Koupéla-Tenkodogo, ainsi que dans les quartiers de Samandin et de Saaba. Ces contrôles ont permis d'intercepter d'importantes quantités de boissons, de cigarettes et de produits pour chicha introduits frauduleusement sur le territoire national, pour une valeur estimée à plusieurs dizaines de millions de francs CFA. Au total, le bilan cumulé de ces interventions menées en moins d'un mois s'élève à 86 430 000 FCFA de marchandises retirées des circuits illégaux. Quand la fraude économique rejoint la menace sécuritaire Pour le Coordonnateur national de la CNLF, la lutte contre la contrebande a franchi un nouveau cap. La fraude ne représente plus uniquement un manque à gagner financier pour l'État ou une concurrence déloyale pour le commerce formel ; lorsqu'elle facilite la circulation clandestine d'explosifs et d'équipements dangereux, elle constitue une préoccupation sécuritaire majeure. Soulignant le sens profond de cette mission, le premier responsable de la CNLF a rappelé l'urgence de cette traque : « Chaque câble détonant intercepté, c’est une vie préservée. Chaque bâton d’explosif saisi, c’est une tragédie évitée ». Face à la persistance de ces trafics, l'organe de contrôle entend maintenir une vigilance rigoureuse sur l'ensemble du réseau national. items.title: Zogbéanta—N’Zérékoré : l’alerte des populations face à un pont en bois fortement dégradé
items.description: À Zogbéanta, dans la sous-préfecture de Palé, préfecture de N’Zérékoré, l’état du pont en bois construit sur le fleuve Oulé suscite de vives inquiétudes. Après plus de cinq années d’utilisation, l’ouvrage est aujourd’hui fortement dégradé et constitue, selon les usagers, un risque pour la circulation sur l’axe Palé-N’Zérékoré. Situé à l’entrée du village de Zogbéanta dans la sous-préfecture de Palé, préfecture de N’Zérékoré, ce pont représente un passage incontournable sur cette route d’environ 36 kilomètres reliant Palé à N’Zérékoré. Mais son état de vétusté, aggravé par les fortes pluies, inquiète de plus en plus les conducteurs, transporteurs et autres usagers. Selon Nèma Loua, président du conseil de district de Zogbéanta, des réparations de fortune sont régulièrement effectuées pour maintenir la circulation, sans toutefois résoudre le problème de fond. « Cinstruit depuis plus de cinq ans, ce pont est aujourd’hui vétuste et n’est plus solide. Par endroits, les citoyens procèdent à des réparations de fortune, juste pour permettre le passage de certains engins et usagers », a-t-il expliqué. La dégradation de l’ouvrage affecte également l’évacuation des produits agricoles de la localité. Café, cacao, riz, huile et légumes seraient notamment confrontés à des difficultés d’acheminement vers les marchés. La situation est particulièrement préoccupante en cette période de grandes pluies. Le président du conseil de district redoute un éventuel effondrement du pont et appelle les autorités à agir avant qu’un accident ne survienne. « Nous sommes exposés au risque d’un effondrement ou d’une rupture du pont », a-t-il alerté. Même inquiétude chez les conducteurs de taxi-moto. Foromo Loua, usager régulier de cet axe, affirme que certains passagers préfèrent descendre des motos avant de traverser le pont à pied, par crainte d’un accident. « Même à vue d’œil, ce pont fait peur. Certaines parties sont endommagées. Même pour nous autres conducteurs, c’est un risque », témoigne-t-il. Face à cette situation, les responsables locaux de Zogbéanta demandent l’intervention rapide de l’État pour remplacer l’actuel ouvrage en bois par un pont durable. Ils sollicitent également l’appui des autorités locales, du gouvernement et des ressortissants de la localité. Pour les usagers, l’enjeu dépasse désormais la simple question de la circulation : il s’agit d’éviter qu’un ouvrage devenu vétuste ne provoque un accident aux conséquences humaines et économiques importantes.

items.title: Burkina: en fin de mission, l’ambassadrice du Canada témoigne sa gratitude à Karamoko Jean-Marie Traoré
items.description: (Ouagadougou, le 16 septembre 2026 Le ministre des Affaires étrangères, le Camarade Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORE, accompagné de la camarade ministre déléguée Bêbgnasgnan Stella Eldine KABRE/KABORE, a reçu en audience ce mercredi 16 septembre 2026, l’ambassadrice du Canada en fin de mission au Burkina Faso. S E Mme Tina GUTHRIE est venue exprimer sa reconnaissance au Chef de la diplomatie et à l’ensemble de son équipe, pour l’accompagnement dont elle a bénéficié au cours de sa mission au Pays des Hommes intègres. La diplomate canadienne a aussi salué une coopération empreinte de confiance entre le Burkina Faso et le Canada, et basée sur le respect mutuel et la défense des valeurs communes. Au terme de sa mission de deux années à Ouagadougou, l’ambassadrice GUTHRIE dit être satisfaite de l’esprit d’ouverture des autorités burkinabè. « Nous avons des points en commun et nous avons aussi des points de divergence, mais on a réussi à échanger ouvertement sur n'importe quel sujet et dans le respect mutuel. Et ça, c'est quelque chose que j'apprécie beaucoup de la part des autorités burkinabè », a-t-elle déclaré à sa sortie d’audience. Elle a également salué l'hospitalité des Burkinabè et leur engagement autour de la cohésion sociale. Le Chef de la diplomatie burkinabè a exprimé sa satisfaction, quant à la collaboration entre son département et l'ambassade du Canada sous le mandat de la diplomate sortante. Tout en souhaitant bon retour à S E Mme Tina GUTHRIE, il a rassuré que c'est avec le même engagement que lui et son équipe vont collaborer avec le nouvel ambassadeur canadien, dont l'accréditation a été acceptée par les autorités burkinabè.
